# pstack engineering pilot

For non-trivial engineering tasks, explicitly load `poteto-mode` (see "Load a skill" under Harness) and choose one playbook. Answer routine questions directly. Read-only requests stay read-only. Keep one checklist in the conversation if the todo tool is unavailable.

This routing takes precedence over playbook steps that repeat a method or exceed the user's scope:

- **Debugging:** Load `root-cause` for root-cause investigation. Carry the repro, cause, and evidence into the playbook; do not repeat the investigation without a reason.
- **TDD:** When a behavior has a practical executable test, use `test-first` as the sole TDD procedure. Skip pstack's separate `tdd` and any duplicate test-first sequence. For Helm or configuration changes without an applicable behavior test, run the relevant targeted validation and state what it does not prove.
- **Planning:** When asked for a plan, spec, or design, or before building a feature, load `spec-first` first, even if `poteto-mode` was not loaded. Specs go to `docs/specs/`, plans to `docs/plans/`; the chat alone is not the plan. Never commit them without authorization. Each stage ends your turn and waits for the user: design, then the written spec, then the plan. A request for "spec and plan" still stops after the spec; write the plan only after the user approves the spec. Approving a design, spec, plan, or summary never authorizes implementation, so never phrase it as "approve and I implement". Implementation needs a separate explicit instruction to implement. Once implementation is authorized, outward actions follow the authorization contract below.
- **Completion:** Load `evidence-before-done` before claiming success. Run the relevant check on the current revision or diff. Reuse fresh evidence for that same artifact; repeat checks only when evidence is stale, incomplete, or independence is requested.

### Playbook crosswalk

When a pstack playbook names a step below, use this workflow's method instead. Do not run both.

| pstack step | This workflow uses |
|---|---|
| Root-cause / reproduce (Bug Fix) | `root-cause`, once; carry its evidence into the fix |
| Failing-test-first / `tdd` | `test-first` as the sole TDD procedure; skip pstack `tdd` |
| Design / spec before a feature or a plan (Feature, Multi-phase plan) | Load `spec-first` and follow its path. An architectural change gets a spec in `docs/specs/`, which the user approves before any plan; a small change gets a short in-chat design |
| Write the plan file | `plan-from-spec`, saved to `docs/plans/` with a link to its spec, then its gap check handoff |
| Plan written, before handing it back | Load `plan-gap-interview` and `grilling` (see "Load a skill" under Harness), plan mode; hand back the plan only after the user approves the summary |
| User adds a requirement, task, or scope change after the spec was approved | Stop at the nearest safe boundary; `plan-gap-interview` change mode updates the spec, then the plan, after approval |
| Verify before done | `evidence-before-done` on the final revision or diff |
| Delegate / swarm / arena workers | Orca `orchestration` when the user asks; otherwise work inline |
| Opening a PR / Shipping / commit / rebase | Authorization contract below: do it when granted, ask when not |
| A playbook or an older plan names `brainstorming`, `writing-plans`, `systematic-debugging`, `test-driven-development`, `verification-before-completion`, or `executing-plans` | Use `spec-first`, `plan-from-spec`, `root-cause`, `test-first`, `evidence-before-done`, or `execution-checkpoint` |
| Default model slugs | The harness model file plus its model escalation, both under Harness |

### Persistent execution checkpoints

For an explicitly approved multi-step implementation plan, load `execution-checkpoint` before editing any code. Initialize a run only if it does not already exist, in the **working repository** (not in this plugin source). The approved plan remains in `docs/plans/`; the execution state is kept under `.pstack/executions/<run-id>/` in that project's repository. Use one stable run ID, shared with the coordinator. No checkpoint is needed for a simple, one-off edit.

At every verified step/task boundary, record the actual tests, evidence, blockers, decisions, summary, and single next action with the skill's `checkpoint.py` CLI. A claimed PASS without executed evidence is not completion. When the session has compacted or restarted, call `resume` first, compare the stored state with the approved plan and actual Git changes, and only then continue from the first unverified task. Do not assume Cursor hooks are a guaranteed in-place compaction signal. When several runs exist, pin `--run` or `PSTACK_RUN_ID` explicitly rather than choosing a recent run. Only one coordinator writes to one run; delegate workers report evidence rather than editing the shared state.

This adds an execution ledger alongside `show-me-your-work`'s decision TSV. Commits, PRs, deployments, and destructive changes follow the authorization contract below.

### Ponytail before and during coding

- Before the first edit, read the affected code and check its callers. Choose the smallest change that meets the acceptance criteria without skipping validation or tests.
- Before adding a function, check whether an existing function, repository pattern, or standard library already covers the need. Add a function only when it has a distinct responsibility or removes real duplication without adding needless indirection.
- While writing, preserve caller contracts, validation, and error handling. Do not add wrappers, options, or abstractions the task does not need.
- For delegated coding, include the change boundary, behavior that must stay intact, and required checks in the worker brief.

## Delegation

Work inline unless the user explicitly requests delegation. If the user requests Orca workers or asks to split code changes across agents, worktrees, or branches, load `orchestration` and follow its Orca dispatch and result loop. Do not silently substitute native subagents if Orca dispatch fails.

pstack still owns the playbook and acceptance criteria. Give each worker a self-contained brief with the goal, phase, isolated write scope, relevant method, behavior to preserve, and required checks.

Every Orca worker runs on an explicit model, chosen in this order: a model the user names for that dispatch, then a worker model the approved spec or plan names, then the `orca workers` line in the Orca model file (see Harness). A named model is a requirement even when it says "if available". Resolve a human name such as "Luna 6" to the exact slug in the Orca model list (see Harness). This overrides the Orca guide's "add `--model` only if the user named one". Start every Orca worker with `python3 "$HOME/.agents/skills/execution-checkpoint/scripts/orca_worker_start.py" [--model <slug>] -- <worker-start args>`, never with a bare `worker-start`. The script checks availability, passes `--model`, reads back the launched model, and stops a worker that runs on anything else. Exit 3 means no requested model is available: stop and ask the user, never fall back to the parent model. Exit 4 means a wrong launch: record a checkpoint blocker and a decision naming the required model before any other dispatch. Brief workers to report the model they ran on.

For native delegation, inherit the parent model if no validated mapping or model override is available. Verify actual worker models before claiming cross-model review.

For Orca, wait for its result notification rather than polling. The parent decides completion from the artifact, commands, and results, not the worker's status alone.

If an Orca start fails, inspect the failed stage and follow the skill's recovery guide. For Codex `agent-hooks-review-prompt`, identify the pending hook source and ask only for the user's trust decision. Never approve it on their behalf or bypass hook trust or sandboxing. Preserve the task and dispatch IDs. After the blocker is resolved, retry the same task with a fresh worker via `--retry-of` when the recovery guide permits it. Do not ask the user to re-enter the brief or keep sending to an unreachable conversation. Require a worker result and evidence, not just a terminal opening.

## Authorization contract

Commits, pushes, PRs, deployments, and other outward actions follow this contract, even when a playbook says otherwise. Authorization comes from three sources; the newest wins:

1. The user's latest instructions in this session.
2. The `## Authorizations` section of the approved spec.
3. `AUTH:` decisions in the execution checkpoint.

A grant stays in force across turns, compaction, and new sessions until the user revokes it. After compaction, reread the spec section and the checkpoint decisions before acting. Never assume a grant was lost.

- **Read the outcome, not the verb.** An instruction authorizes every routine step needed to reach the outcome it names. "Fix it and report when it is ready for review", "prepare it for review", or "open an MR" means: commit to a work branch, push that branch, open or update a draft MR/PR, update the linked ticket, then report the link.
- **A go covers the whole question.** When the user answers a permission question with a go, or with "don't ask", it covers every action named in that question and the same actions for the rest of the task.
- **Act, then report.** Do authorized actions and report what you did, with links and evidence. Never ask "may I commit / push / open the MR / continue?" for an authorized action.
- **Default grants.** Once the user has told you to implement an approved plan, these are granted unless the spec forbids them:
  - commit on a non-default work branch;
  - push that branch, without force;
  - open or update a draft MR/PR;
  - update linked tickets;
  - run read-only commands against cloud, CI, and issue trackers.
- **Keep going.** After a verified step, start the next plan step when it is within the grants. Do not ask "shall I continue?". End the turn only when one of these holds:
  - you are waiting on an action only the user may take;
  - you hit a blocker;
  - a decision is needed that the spec does not settle;
  - the work is done.
- **Ask first,** unless the user granted that exact action for that item. Examples of an exact grant: "after I merge, run the apply job", "start the instance with gcloud". These actions need it:
  - merge;
  - apply or deploy;
  - push to the default or a protected branch;
  - changes to production or shared environments;
  - anything the spec lists as forbidden or ask-first.
- **Always ask,** even when a grant seems to cover it:
  - force push or history rewrite;
  - deleting branches, data, or resources;
  - any change that destroys or replaces a resource;
  - approving hooks or trust prompts.
- **Record grants when they are given.** When the user grants or revokes a permission mid-task, do these two steps without an interview, then continue; the user's statement is the approval:
  - update the spec's `## Authorizations` section;
  - when a checkpoint run exists, record it with `checkpoint.py decision --text "AUTH: <action and scope>" --reason "user, <date>"`.
- **Workers.** Give delegated workers the grants that apply to their slice in the brief.

Tool permission prompts and safety hooks still apply. Do not substitute another tool to bypass them.

## Harness: Antigravity

- **Tools.** Ask structured questions with `ask_question`. Spawn native subagents with `invoke_subagent`. Keep the checklist with `update_steps`. Run shell commands with `run_command`. A skill that names the `question` tool means `ask_question`; one that names the `subagent` or `task` tool means `invoke_subagent`.
- **Load a skill.** Antigravity has no skill tool. Read the skill's `SKILL.md` with `read_file`, from `~/.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` or the path listed in your available skills, and follow it. "Load `X`" anywhere in these rules or in a skill means this.
- **Model file.** pstack skills read `~/.agents/pstack-models.antigravity.md`. Wherever a skill names `~/.agents/pstack-models.md` as the settings file for "other harnesses", use the Antigravity file instead. `/setup-pstack` fills it from `agy models`.
- **Orca model file and list.** Orca workers run OpenCode in every harness. Use the `orca workers` line in `~/.agents/pstack-models.md` (the OpenCode file), and take exact slugs from `opencode models`.
- **Permission gates.** The `pstack-gate` hook asks before commit, push, PR, Helm, kubectl, and Terraform commands. Do not route around a gate with another tool.

### Model escalation

The user selects the parent model with `/model` or `agy --model`. Do not switch the session automatically. When a role in the model file names a model, recommend that model for the matching playbook (`bug-fix` for Bug Fix, `hillclimb` for Hillclimb and Swarm, `feature, refactoring` for feature, refactoring, and performance work). When it says `inherit-parent`, stay on the current model. If the first result fails verification after a targeted check, or the task turns out to span multiple components, suggest the highest-effort variant of the same family that `agy models` lists.
